subject: pathology
title: Chemokine Families, Endothelial Nitric Oxide, and Leukocyte Homing

steps.tx: Chemokines represent a vast superfamily of small eight- to ten-kilodalton structurally homologous cytokines that function primarily as chemoattractants for specific leukocyte subsets. Possessing conserved cysteine residues that form internal disulfide bonds, **chemokines direct leukocyte trafficking** during homeostatic immune surveillance and recruit inflammatory cells to sites of injury.
steps.say: Chemokines are small structural proteins with conserved cysteines that direct leukocyte trafficking.

left.title: Inflammatory Chemokines
points: Induced transcriptionally by TNF, IL-1, and microbial endotoxins
Attract neutrophils, monocytes, and effector lymphocytes to injury
Examples: CXCL8 (IL-8), CCL2 (MCP-1), CCL3 (MIP-1-alpha)
Concentrated locally by binding endothelial heparan sulfate chains

right.title: Homeostatic Chemokines
points: Constitutively produced within lymphoid and non-lymphoid tissues
Regulate baseline physiological leukocyte and lymphocyte migration
Direct naive T and B lymphocytes to distinct zones in lymph nodes
Examples: CXCL12 (SDF-1) for stem cells, CCL19/CCL21 for T-cells

steps.tx: Chemokines are classified into four distinct structural families based on the arrangement of their amino-terminal cysteine residues. In the **CXC chemokine family**, the first two cysteines are separated by an intervening amino acid, exemplified by interleukin-eight (CXCL8), which specifically activates and recruits neutrophils to acute pyogenic inflammatory foci.
steps.say: CXC chemokines have cysteines separated by an amino acid, exemplified by neutrophil-attracting CXCL8.

nodes.label: Tissue Macrophages Encountering Bacteria Secrete CXCL8 (Interleukin-8)
Binds Heparan Sulfate on Luminal Endothelium, Creating Solid-Phase Gradient
Rolling Neutrophils Engage CXCR1 and CXCR2 G-Protein-Coupled Receptors
Activates Integrins and Directs Rapid Chemotactic Transmigration

steps.tx: In the CC chemokine family, the first two amino-terminal cysteines are directly adjacent without an intervening residue. Members including **monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (CCL2)**, macrophage inflammatory protein-one alpha, and eotaxin (CCL11) specifically attract monocytes, eosinophils, basophils, and lymphocytes rather than neutrophils.
steps.say: CC chemokines have adjacent cysteines that recruit monocytes, eosinophils, and lymphocytes.

left.title: CXC Chemokines (Alpha Subfamily)
points: First two cysteines separated by one amino acid (C-X-C)
Act predominantly on neutrophils (if containing ELR sequence)
Major prototype is CXCL8 (interleukin-8)
Drives rapid neutrophilic consolidation in bacterial infections

right.title: CC Chemokines (Beta Subfamily)
points: First two cysteines are directly adjacent (C-C motif)
Act on monocytes, lymphocytes, eosinophils, and basophils
Prototypes: CCL2 (MCP-1), CCL5 (RANTES), CCL11 (eotaxin)
Drives chronic mononuclear infiltration, atherosclerosis, and allergy

steps.tx: A soluble, highly diffusible free radical gas synthesized from L-arginine by nitric oxide synthases modulates multiple microvascular events in inflammation. Synthesized by endothelial cells, **endothelial nitric oxide (NO)** diffuses into underlying vascular smooth muscle cells, activating soluble guanylyl cyclase to elevate cyclic GMP and induce profound arteriolar relaxation.
steps.say: Endothelial nitric oxide elevates cyclic GMP in vascular smooth muscle, causing profound vasodilation.

nodes.label: Shear Stress or Histamine Activates Endothelial Nitric Oxide Synthase (eNOS)
Synthesizes Paracrine Gas Nitric Oxide (NO) from Substrate L-Arginine
NO Diffuses into Vascular Smooth Muscle, Activating Soluble Guanylyl Cyclase
Elevated Cyclic GMP Activates Protein Kinase G, Inducing Vasodilation

steps.tx: Endothelium makes a soluble free radical gas from L arginine. **Endothelial nitric oxide** diffuses into the smooth muscle beneath, turns on soluble guanylyl cyclase, raises cyclic GMP, and relaxes the arteriole. At rest that same nitric oxide also keeps leukocytes from sticking to the endothelial surface, so the vessel stays dilated and relatively non adhesive until inflammation shuts the signal down. Loss of this basal release favours both vasospasm and inappropriate leukocyte adhesion.
steps.say: Endothelial nitric oxide is made from L arginine and diffuses into vascular smooth muscle, where cyclic GMP rises and the arteriole relaxes. In resting endothelium the same gas discourages leukocytes from adhering. When that basal output falls, vessels constrict more readily and white cells stick more easily.

vis.alt: Resting endothelium releasing nitric oxide that relaxes smooth muscle and keeps leukocytes from adhering.
vis.caption: Nitric oxide leaves resting endothelium, relaxes the arteriole beneath, and discourages leukocytes from sticking. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: One mediator keeps leukocytes off the wall instead of calling them onto it. **Nitric oxide** from endothelium relaxes smooth muscle and inhibits leukocyte adhesion and platelet clumping, so inflamed vessels must lower it locally before cells can stick. That restraint explains why endothelial dysfunction tilts tissue toward thrombosis and persistent inflammation together. In sepsis the same gas made in excess collapses vascular tone, showing its power from the opposite direction.
steps.say: Endothelial nitric oxide relaxes vessels and inhibits leukocyte adhesion. Losing it locally lets inflammation and thrombosis proceed together.

vis.alt: Image showing nitric oxide inhibiting leukocyte adhesion to endothelium.
vis.caption: Nitric oxide is shown keeping leukocytes from adhering to a vessel wall. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Under resting baseline conditions, continuous basal endothelial nitric oxide production functions as an endogenous anti-inflammatory safeguard. By inducing vascular smooth muscle relaxation and preventing leukocyte sticking, baseline NO **inhibits leukocyte adhesion to endothelium**, suppresses platelet aggregation, and actively scavenges reactive oxygen species in resting microvessels.
steps.say: Baseline endothelial nitric oxide relaxes vessels and inhibits leukocyte adhesion and platelet aggregation.

vis.alt: Endothelial nitric oxide at rest relaxing smooth muscle and inhibiting leukocyte adhesion to endothelium
vis.caption: Endothelial nitric oxide at rest relaxing smooth muscle and inhibiting leukocyte adhesion to endothelium. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: When macrophages and endothelial cells are stimulated by microbial lipopolysaccharide and interferon-gamma, they express the inducible isoform of nitric oxide synthase. Producing copious, sustained amounts of nitric oxide, **inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS)** generates reactive nitrogen intermediates that combine with superoxide to form bactericidal peroxynitrite radicals.
steps.say: Macrophage iNOS produces copious nitric oxide that forms microbicidal peroxynitrite to kill pathogens.

left.title: Endothelial NOS (eNOS / NOS3)
points: Constitutively expressed in vascular endothelial cells
Calcium-calmodulin dependent; activated transiently by shear stress
Produces low nanomolar physiological pulses of nitric oxide
Maintains basal arteriolar vasodilation and prevents thrombosis

right.title: Inducible NOS (iNOS / NOS2)
points: Transcriptionally induced by cytokines (IFN-gamma, TNF) and LPS
Calcium-independent; remains active for hours to days once expressed
Produces high micromolar cytotoxic bursts of nitric oxide
Microbicidal against intracellular pathogens; contributes to septic shock

steps.tx: Systemic release of inflammatory cytokines drives coordinated alterations in hepatic protein synthesis termed the acute-phase response. Under intense interleukin-six stimulation, hepatocytes downregulate albumin synthesis while massively upregulating essential **acute phase reactants**, including C-reactive protein, serum amyloid A, fibrinogen, haptoglobin, and hepcidin.
steps.say: Cytokines induce the hepatic acute-phase response, switching protein synthesis from albumin to CRP and fibrinogen.

nodes.label: Macrophage IL-6, IL-1, and TNF Enter the Portal and Systemic Circulation
Hepatocytes Reprogram Transcription via STAT3 and NF-Kappa-B
Massive Upregulation of CRP, Serum Amyloid A, Fibrinogen, and Ferritin
Downregulation of Albumin, Transferrin, and Transthyretin Synthesis

steps.tx: Elevations in circulating acute-phase reactants provide vital clinical diagnostic and prognostic tools. Serum C-reactive protein monitors ongoing inflammation and treatment response, elevated fibrinogen accelerates red cell rouleaux formation to elevate the erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and serum amyloid A can deposit chronically as **secondary AA amyloidosis**.
steps.say: Acute-phase proteins serve as clinical inflammatory biomarkers and can deposit as AA amyloid in chronic disease.
